primary.label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling
primary.rationale: The talk centers on agent loop architecture, the exit-condition problem, validation-error retries, and type-safe tool definitions within the Pydantic AI harness. Pydantic AI is a developer framework for building type-safe agents, with general-purpose demonstration examples. Content covers building agents from scratch and debugging failed agent runs with Logfire tracing. Requires prior knowledge of Pydantic, Python type checking, LLMs, and structured output concepts. summary: Samuel Colvin delivers a talk on building AI applications the Pydantic way, adapted from his PyCon presentation. He explicitly states he cannot cover the originally advertised topic of Human-seeded Evals due to time limitations. The talk focuses on type safety as a foundational practice for building reliable, scalable GenAI applications, arguing it enables confident refactoring—especially important since no one knows their AI application's final shape at the outset. He notes type safety also helps coding agents like Cursor self-verify their work, a capability absent in frameworks like LangChain and LangGraph, which he criticizes for lacking type safety. Colvin reviews the now-standard definition of an agent (environment, tools, system prompt, while loop calling the LLM), attributing it to Barry Zang's AI Engineer talk and the Anthropic definition adopted by OpenAI and Google's ADK. He highlights a real problem: the pseudocode lacks an exit condition, and deciding when to end an agent loop is nontrivial, with strategies including plain-text returns, final result tools, and structured output types. He demonstrates Pydantic AI with a minimal structured-data extraction example, then shows the agentic loop's value when a field validator rejects a date of birth (requiring pre-1900), causing the validation error to be returned to the model for a corrected retry—visible in Logfire as two Gemini calls. He explains type-safe generics for output types and dependencies (deps), claiming Pydantic AI is the only agent framework investing this heavily in type safety. A memory-tools demo (record_memory/retrieve_memory) initially fails due to a substring-match mismatch, which Logfire reveals; a second attempt succeeds. He closes noting Logfire provides per-span and aggregate tracing with pricing, though time runs out before covering MCP or evals.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and Scope
sections.summary: Colvin introduces the talk as adapted from his PyCon presentation on building AI applications the Pydantic way, and notes he will not be able to cover evals due to time constraints.

sections.title: Type Safety and Framework Critique
sections.summary: Colvin argues type safety is essential for building reliable, refactorable AI applications and for enabling coding agents like Cursor to self-verify. He criticizes LangChain and LangGraph for not being type-safe.

sections.title: Agent Definition and Exit Problem
sections.summary: Reviews the standard agent definition (environment, tools, system prompt, while loop) attributed to Barry Zang/Anthropic. Highlights the missing exit condition in pseudocode and discusses strategies for ending agent loops.

sections.title: Minimal Pydantic AI Demo
sections.summary: Demonstrates a minimal Pydantic AI example extracting a Person model with three fields from unstructured text, noting it could scale to large documents and complex nested schemas.

sections.title: Agentic Loop with Validation Retry
sections.summary: Shows the agentic loop's value by adding a field validator requiring DOB before 1900. The model initially returns 1987, triggers a validation error, which is returned to the model for a corrected retry. Logfire reveals two Gemini calls.

sections.title: Type Safety in Outputs and Dependencies
sections.summary: Explains how Pydantic AI's generic output type provides both static typing and runtime validation. Introduces the deps generic for type-safe tool dependencies, claiming Pydantic AI is the only framework investing this heavily in type safety.

sections.title: Tools and Memory Demo
sections.summary: Demonstrates long-term memory tools (record_memory and retrieve_memory) with type-safe deps. The demo uses Postgres/Docker and initially fails, which Colvin uses to demonstrate Logfire's debugging value.

sections.title: Logfire Debugging and Conclusion
sections.summary: Uses Logfire to debug the failed demo, revealing a substring-match mismatch ('your name' vs 'user's name is Samuel'). A second attempt succeeds. Notes Logfire provides tracing durations and pricing per span and aggregate. Concludes due to time.

limitations: Human-seeded Evals topic not covered due to time constraints despite being the advertised title

Type-safe setup is not necessarily trivial for users and requires some additional work
